head: acf455cb3e33259ce8887672f3fe679659161180
scope: All four planned B14 candidates were reviewed in separate bounded batches. This is audit completion, not repaired implementation or release/live acceptance.

findings.title: Sample authorization time after entering the Store transaction
findings.trigger: Call check_context or check_capability while now < the grant/session/context expiry, then let Store acquisition wait until now >= that expiry before invoking the transaction closure.
findings.observed: All six guard/expiry combinations return Ok(()) instead of Err(Expired). Positive controls succeed before the wait; already-expired controls and read with transaction-local time deny correctly.
findings.effect: Expired context/capability checks can authorize after Store contention. Direct executor callers use check_context before guest bootstrap/final-output delivery and check_capability before broker operations.
findings.limit: Reproduced against the unchanged runtime with a deterministic injected Store/Clock, not a live native SQLite queue. Native epoch/revocation checks still use current ledger state; this finding does not establish unauthorized persisted writes. No executor exploit or live runtime acceptance is claimed.
findings.suggestedAction: Borrow self.clock before transaction, then call clock.now_ms() inside each transaction closure before bound_context, matching read/create_session/host_context. Add permanent delayed-admission regressions for both methods and all expiry sources; rerun runtime and direct executor tests.

findings.title: Propagate native session-close errors before acknowledging command cancellation
findings.trigger: A running task is canceled while the SQLite transaction that closes its native session fails before COMMIT. A previously admitted relay reaches its blocking broker after the cancel response and storage becomes writable again.
findings.observed: cancel_install discards authority.with(host_end_session) errors and returns unit. plugin_command_cancel consequently returns Ok(()). The failed transaction retains the session/context; after the injected SQLite failure is cleared, the unchanged state.set arm returns version 1 and the late value is persisted.
findings.effect: The user receives a successful cancellation acknowledgement while old native write authority remains usable by already admitted work. This violates the documented close-before-ACK contract. Normal cancellation closes the session and denies the same late write.
findings.limit: Reproduced with the unchanged extracted cancellation method, product-command body and state.set arm, actual runtime and actual SQLite adapter. Native/view setup is headless and the already admitted relay is simulated; no actual WebView race or exploit was executed. The demonstrated late write is confined to the installation namespace, not canonical host library data.
findings.suggestedAction: Make cancel_install return a Result and propagate poisoned-task-lock/session-close failures. Return success from plugin_command_cancel only after every matching session/context has durably closed. Keep already admitted work unable to commit after successful cancellation; cover failure and successful controls with permanent regressions.

evidenceValidity.result: All original scoped hashes still match; previous findings and passed scopes remain valid.

limits: B14-R01 and B14-N01 remain unrepaired and lack permanent regressions.
A real WebView/IPC cancellation race and actual admitted desktop execution were not run.
